Beijing.text: In 2022 China's capital became the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Olympics.
Beijing.evidence: In 2022, Beijing became the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Olympics, and also the Summer and Winter Paralympics.

Tokyo.text: Originally Edo, Japan's capital was renamed Tokyo ('Eastern Capital') when the emperor moved there from Kyoto.
Tokyo.evidence: After the Meiji Restoration (1868), the imperial capital in Kyoto was moved to Edo, and the city was renamed Tokyo (lit. 'Eastern Capital').

Kinshasa.text: DR Congo's capital faces Brazzaville across the Congo River: the world's closest pair of capital cities.
Kinshasa.evidence: Across the river sits Brazzaville, the smaller capital of the neighboring Republic of the Congo, forming the world's closest pair of capital cities despite being separated by a four-kilometer-wide unbridged span of the Congo River.

Jakarta.text: The Dutch East India Company seized Indonesia's capital in 1619 and rebuilt it as Batavia.
Jakarta.evidence: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) seized Jayakarta in 1619 and rebuilt it as Batavia, its main administrative centre in Asia and an important trading port.

Dhaka.text: Bangladesh's capital has more rickshaws than any city, over 1.5 million a day, though only about 220,000 are licensed.
Dhaka.evidence: Cycle rickshaws and CNG auto-rickshaws are the main modes of transport within the metro area, with more than 1.5 million rickshaws running each day: the highest number in any city in the world. However, only around 220 thousand rickshaws are licensed by the city government.

Lima.text: Around one-third of Peru's population lives in its metropolitan area.
Lima.evidence: Around one-third of the national population now lives in its metropolitan area.

Cairo.text: Egypt's capital is known as "the city of a thousand minarets" for its wealth of Islamic architecture.
Cairo.evidence: Cairo has since become a longstanding centre of political and cultural life, and is titled "the city of a thousand minarets" for its preponderance of Islamic architecture.

Seoul.text: During the Korean War South Korea's capital changed hands four times.
Seoul.evidence: The Korean War brought fierce battles, with Seoul changing hands four times and leaving the city mostly in ruins.

Mexico City.text: Mexico's capital began as Tenochtitlan, a Mexica city built around 1325 on islands in Lake Texcoco.
Mexico City.evidence: It began as Tenochtitlan, a Mexica city built around 1325 on islands in Lake Texcoco.

London.text: The UK's capital has the world's oldest rapid transit system, the London Underground.
London.evidence: The London Underground is the world's oldest rapid transit system.
